To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cost of antiretrovials was reduced by 40% with the use of treatment interruptions in patients with a high CD4 count and that the cost of adverse events and consultations was not higher with treatment interruptions.
the cost of HAARR was reduced in the IT arm compared with the CT arm and that the difference was due to the difference between the cost of the drugs used in the 2 arms.
a 40% cost reduction of HAART medications was observed in patients who interrupted their treatment for 16 weeks every 8 weeks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic evaluation of the ANRS (Agence Nationale de Recherche sur le Sida) 106 Window study.
the costs of treatment interruption strategies in the setting of the ANRS-106 Window trial.
the costs and cost savings of intermittent versus continuous antiretrovirals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of IT in patients with a controlled HIV infection can reduce the total cost of care by approximately 40%, mainly due to the reduction of HAART cost.
IT is a cost-effective strategy in terms of the total cost of HIV treatment.
treatment interruption is not a cost-saving strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of IT in the context of a structured treatment interruption strategy is a cost-saving strategy.

the use of an 8-week on, 8-week off treatment interruption strategy is associated with a significant reduction in total medical care costs compared with the continuous use of highly active antiretoviral therapy.
IT was not only a cost-saving strategy but also a cost-effective strategy in patients with controlled HIV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of IT in the setting of chronic HIV infection can reduce the total cost of antiretrov viral therapy.
treatment interruption is a cost-saving strategy for patients with controlled HIV infection.
the reduction of HAART costs by 40% is not associated with an increase in the costs related to hospitalizations, consultations, or other adverse events.
